tools.name: basecamp_list_projects
tools.description:
List the active projects visible to the configured Basecamp account, with the ID you need for every other tool in this server.

Args:
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: one entry per project with its name, numeric ID, description, the names of the dock tools that are enabled on it (todoset, message_board, vault, chat, schedule, ...) and a browser URL. Start here when you know a project only by name — the numeric ID it returns is what basecamp_list_todolists, basecamp_list_messages and the rest expect.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_get_project
tools.description:
Fetch one project in full, including its complete dock — the list of tools attached to it with their individual IDs and enabled state.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project's numeric ID.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: the project's name, purpose, status, description and browser URL, then every dock entry (todoset, message_board, vault, chat, schedule, questionnaire, inbox) with its ID and whether it is enabled. Use this to check whether a project actually has, say, a message board before calling basecamp_create_message against it.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_project
tools.description:
Create a new Basecamp project.

Args:
  name (str, required): the project name. Plain text, not HTML — it is stored and shown verbatim, the same way a to-do's content is.
  description (str, optional): the subtitle shown under the name on the projects page. Plain text as well.

Returns: the new project's ID, browser URL and full dock, so the todoset/message board/vault IDs are available without a follow-up basecamp_get_project.

A new project has a To-dos tool but no lists inside it, so creating a to-do takes two more steps: basecamp_create_todolist, then basecamp_create_todo. Each call creates a separate project — Basecamp allows two projects with the same name.

name.description: Project name. Plain text, not HTML — entities are stored and shown literally.

description.description: Optional subtitle shown under the project name. Plain text.

tools.name: basecamp_update_project
tools.description:
Rename a project or change its description.

Basecamp's API clears any field you omit, so this tool reads the project first and resends its current value for whichever field you did not supply — a partial update stays partial, the same way basecamp_update_todo works.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project to change.
  name (str, optional): new name. Plain text, not HTML.
  description (str, optional): new subtitle. Pass an empty string to clear it.

Returns: the project's updated name, description and browser URL. This changes the project's own fields only — it does not touch its to-dos, messages or documents.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

name.description: New project name. Plain text, not HTML.

description.description: New subtitle; pass an empty string to clear it.

tools.name: basecamp_list_todolists
tools.description:
List the to-do lists inside a project's To-dos tool. A project's to-dos are grouped into lists, so this is the step between a project and its individual to-dos.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project's numeric ID.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each list's name, ID, description, completion ratio and browser URL. Pass a returned list ID to basecamp_list_todos or basecamp_create_todo. Errors clearly if the project has no To-dos tool enabled.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_todolist
tools.description:
Create a new to-do list in a project's To-dos tool.

Resolves the project's todoset automatically — pass only the project ID. A project's
To-dos tool starts empty, so create a list here before adding to-dos with
basecamp_create_todo.

Args:
  - project_id (number): Basecamp project ID (from basecamp_list_projects)
  - name (string): The list name — required
  - description (string): Optional longer body (HTML allowed)

Returns: the created list's id, name and app_url. Use the id with basecamp_create_todo.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

tools.name: basecamp_list_todos
tools.description:
List the to-dos inside one to-do list. Open to-dos are returned by default; completed ones are a separate archive you have to ask for.

Args:
  todolist_id (int, required): the list's numeric ID, from basecamp_list_todolists.
  completed (bool, optional): false (default) returns open to-dos; true returns the completed ones instead — it is a switch, not an inclusion flag.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each to-do's title, ID, assignees, due date, comment count and browser URL. The IDs it returns are what basecamp_complete_todo, basecamp_list_comments and basecamp_create_comment take.

completed.description: true returns completed to-dos instead of open ones. Default false.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_todo
tools.description:
Add a new to-do to an existing to-do list.

Args:
  todolist_id (int, required): the list to add to, from basecamp_list_todolists.
  content (str, required): the to-do's title — the one line people see. Plain text, not HTML: it is stored and displayed verbatim, so "A & B" shows up as "A & B", not "A & B". Write the literal characters you want. This differs from description.
  description (str, optional): longer notes. Basic HTML is accepted, and HTML entities are rendered — the opposite of content.
  assignee_ids (int[], optional): people to assign, by ID from basecamp_list_people.
  due_on (str, optional): due date as YYYY-MM-DD.
  notify (bool, optional): true emails the assignees. Default false, so assigning someone does not ping them unless you ask.

Returns: the created to-do's ID, title, assignees, due date and browser URL. Each call creates a separate to-do — calling it twice with the same title makes two.

todolist_id.description: To-do list ID to add the to-do to.

content.description: The to-do's title. Plain text, not HTML — entities like & are stored and shown literally.

description.description: Optional longer description; basic HTML allowed, unlike content.

assignee_ids.description: Optional person IDs to assign, from basecamp_list_people.

due_on.description: Optional due date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

notify.description: true emails the assignees about the new to-do. Default false.

tools.name: basecamp_complete_todo
tools.description:
Mark a to-do as completed, or reopen one that was already completed.

Args:
  todo_id (int, required): the to-do's numeric ID, from basecamp_list_todos.
  completed (bool, optional): true (default) completes it; false reopens it.

Returns: a confirmation of the new state. Setting a to-do to the state it is already in is harmless — this sets a flag rather than toggling one, so it is safe to retry.

completed.description: true completes the to-do (default); false reopens it.

tools.name: basecamp_update_todo
tools.description:
Change an existing to-do's title, description, assignees or dates.

Only pass the fields you want to change. Basecamp's own API clears any field you omit,
so this tool reads the to-do first and resends its current values for everything you
did not supply — a partial update stays partial.

To deliberately clear a date, pass null for due_on or starts_on. To clear all
assignees, pass an empty array for assignee_ids.

Args:
  - todo_id (number): The to-do ID (from basecamp_list_todos)
  - content (string): New title. Plain text, not HTML — it is stored verbatim, so an
    entity like & stays "&" on screen. description is the opposite: HTML there
    is rendered.
  - description (string): New body (HTML allowed)
  - assignee_ids (number[]): Replacement assignee list (from basecamp_list_people); [] clears
  - due_on (string | null): New due date YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear
  - starts_on (string | null): New start date YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear
  - notify (boolean): Whether to notify assignees (default: false)

Returns: the updated to-do's id, content, due_on, assignee names and app_url.

content.description: New title. Plain text, not HTML — entities are stored and shown literally.

description.description: New body, HTML allowed, unlike content

assignee_ids.description: Replacement assignee IDs; empty array clears all assignees

due_on.description: New due date YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear

starts_on.description: New start date YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear

tools.name: basecamp_move_todo
tools.description:
Move a to-do into a different to-do list, or reorder it within the one it is in.

The to-do keeps its ID, comments, assignees, dates and completion history. That makes this
the tool for restructuring a project — deleting and recreating a to-do loses all of it.

The destination list has to be in the same project. Basecamp returns an empty body from
this call and ignores a destination it does not accept rather than reporting an error, so
the tool re-reads the to-do afterwards and fails loudly if it did not land where you asked.

Args:
  - todo_id (number): The to-do ID (from basecamp_list_todos)
  - todolist_id (number): Destination list (from basecamp_list_todolists). Omit to reorder
    the to-do within its current list.
  - position (number): 1-based position in the destination list, 1 = top. Omit on a move
    and the to-do goes to the top.

Pass todolist_id, position, or both — one of them is required.

Returns: the to-do's title, the list it now sits in, its position, and its browser URL.

todolist_id.description: Destination to-do list ID, in the same project. Omit to reorder within the current list.

position.description: 1-based position, 1 = top. Omit on a move to land at the top.

tools.name: basecamp_delete_todo
tools.description:
Delete a to-do by moving it to the project's trash.

Basecamp has no permanent delete through the API. This sets the to-do's status to
trashed: it disappears from the to-do list, and Basecamp keeps it recoverable from the
project's trash for a limited period (about 30 days) before purging it. An admin can
restore it from the Basecamp UI in the meantime.

Args:
  - todo_id (number): The to-do ID (from basecamp_list_todos)

Returns: a confirmation that the to-do was trashed.

tools.name: basecamp_list_messages
tools.description:
List the posts on a project's message board, newest first.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project's numeric ID.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each post's subject, ID, author, date, comment count and browser URL — a listing only, without the post bodies. Pass an ID to basecamp_get_message to read one in full. Errors clearly if the project has no message board enabled.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_get_message
tools.description:
Read one message board post in full, with its body converted from Basecamp's rich text to plain text.

Args:
  message_id (int, required): the post's numeric ID, from basecamp_list_messages.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: subject, author, date, comment count, browser URL and the full body text. Comments are not included — fetch those with basecamp_list_comments using the same ID.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_message
tools.description:
Post a new message to a project's message board. Posting an active message notifies the project's subscribers, so use draft mode when you are preparing something for a human to review first.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project to post in.
  subject (str, required): the post's title.
  content (str, optional): the body. Basic HTML is accepted.
  draft (bool, optional): true saves an unpublished draft; false (default) publishes it.

Returns: the new post's ID, subject, status and browser URL. Each call creates a separate post.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

content.description: Optional message body; basic HTML allowed.

draft.description: true saves it as an unpublished draft instead of posting. Default false.

tools.name: basecamp_list_documents
tools.description:
List the documents in a project's Docs & Files vault.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project's numeric ID.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each document's title, ID, author, date, comment count and browser URL — titles only, without the document bodies. Pass an ID to basecamp_get_document to read one. This covers the vault's top level; uploads and subfolders are not listed. Errors clearly if the project has no Docs & Files tool enabled.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_get_document
tools.description:
Read one document in full, with its body converted from Basecamp's rich text to plain text.

Args:
  document_id (int, required): the document's numeric ID, from basecamp_list_documents.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: title, author, created and updated timestamps, comment count, browser URL and the full body text. Comments are not included — fetch those with basecamp_list_comments using the same ID.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_document
tools.description:
Create a document in a project's Docs & Files vault.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project to create the document in.
  title (str, required): the document's title.
  content (str, required): the document body. Basic HTML is accepted.
  draft (bool, optional): true saves it as a draft; false (default) publishes it.

Returns: the new document's ID, title, status and browser URL. Each call creates a separate document.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

content.description: The document body; basic HTML allowed.

draft.description: true saves it as a draft instead of publishing. Default false.

tools.name: basecamp_list_chat_lines
tools.description:
Read the recent lines from a project's Campfire chat room, newest first.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project's numeric ID.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each line's author, timestamp, ID and text. Campfire keeps a rolling window rather than a full archive, so this is recent chat, not project history. Errors clearly if the project has no Campfire enabled.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_post_chat_line
tools.description:
Post a line to a project's Campfire chat room. This is immediately visible to everyone in the project and cannot be edited afterwards, so treat it as sending a chat message rather than saving a draft.

Args:
  project_id (int, required): the project whose Campfire to post in.
  content (str, required): the message text. Basic HTML is accepted.

Returns: a confirmation with the new line's ID. Each call posts a separate line.

project_id.description: Basecamp project ID, as returned by basecamp_list_projects.

content.description: The chat message text; basic HTML allowed.

tools.name: basecamp_list_comments
tools.description:
List the comments on any commentable Basecamp record — a to-do, a message board post or a document all use the same recording ID space.

Args:
  recording_id (int, required): the ID of the to-do, message or document to read comments on, exactly as returned by the corresponding list or get tool.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each comment's author, timestamp, ID and text.

recording_id.description: ID of the to-do, message or document whose comments you want.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_create_comment
tools.description:
Add a comment to any commentable Basecamp record — a to-do, a message board post or a document. Comments notify the record's subscribers.

Args:
  recording_id (int, required): the ID of the to-do, message or document to comment on.
  content (str, required): the comment text. Basic HTML is accepted.

Returns: the new comment's ID and browser URL. Each call adds a separate comment.

recording_id.description: ID of the to-do, message or document to comment on.

content.description: The comment text; basic HTML allowed.

tools.name: basecamp_list_people
tools.description:
List people in the Basecamp account, or just the ones on a single project.

Args:
  project_id (int, optional): when given, lists only the people with access to that project; when omitted, lists everyone in the account.
  page (int, optional): 1-based page of results, default 1.
  limit (int, optional): roughly how many items to gather across pages before stopping, default 50. Basecamp pages at 15 and honours no page-size parameter, so this is done by following pages here.
  response_format (str, optional): 'markdown' (default) or 'json'.

Returns: each person's name, ID, email address, job title and whether they are an admin, an owner or a client. The IDs it returns are what basecamp_create_todo takes as assignee_ids.

project_id.description: Optional project ID; omit to list everyone in the account.

page.description: 1-based page number. Responses report the next page when more results exist.

limit.description: Roughly how many items to gather before stopping, across as many 15-record pages as that takes (default 50). Raise it to pull a long list in one call instead of paging by hand; the response still reports a next page when more remain.

response_format.description: Output shape: 'markdown' for readable prose (default), 'json' for raw records.

tools.name: basecamp_whoami
tools.description:
Show which Basecamp identity this server is acting as.

Args: none.

Returns: the authenticated person's name, ID, email address and admin/owner flags. Useful as a credentials check before a write, and to know whose name will appear on to-dos, messages and comments this server creates.
